Create an independent reference-guided photographic stress test in which the selected random complex concept makes the ample body, broad sleeves, layered structure, and embroidered neckline of a West African grand boubou visibly judgeable.

Create a full-length photorealistic civic-fashion editorial: a nighttime concrete-atrium scene built around a West African grand boubou silhouette during an architecture biennale installation. The subject is the same adult woman shown in the supplied portrait reference. Her facial structure, eye aperture and spacing, nose, lips, jawline, adult age, and long dark hair remain faithfully matched to that reference. She wears a floor-length grand boubou with an ample rectangular body, broad open sleeves, and dense embroidery framing the neck and center front over a coordinated inner wrapper. She catches a falling paper architecture model against one forearm while the opposite sleeve opens into a full drape, making the robe's volume and layered construction readable. Show both sleeve apertures, the continuous shoulder-to-body expanse, embroidered neckline, center-front panel, inner-layer glimpse, and lower hem together. Use full-body architectural framing, luminous concrete, warm installation light, cool skylight spill, natural skin texture, and sharply resolved textile weight.

candidates.interpreted_meaning: An adult fashion relation in which a low garment neckline defines a visible region spanning the lower neck, clavicles, shoulders, and upper chest without requiring an intermammary cleavage line.

A full-body spiral pose in which an offset support or lifted free foot initiates a three-dimensional chain of opposed pelvis, ribcage, shoulder, arm, and head directions that remains legible through depth rather than as a flat S silhouette.

A West African grand boubou is an expansive outer garment whose near-rectangular cloth body produces very broad sleeve openings and a continuous shoulder-to-body volume, often focused by embroidery around the neck or center front and worn with a coordinated inner garment or wrapper. Regional and gendered forms vary; volume, embroidery, color, or a generic robe alone is not sufficient, and agbada remains a related but separately named ensemble.
